summary: Four blocking gaps remain: upgrades retain removed managed assets and configuration; the active SPEC cannot pass its own committed-task prerequisite and lacks terminal homologation; and the installed-set and unknown-command tests do not exercise the contracts they claim to prove.

evidence: Preserved command, runtime and browserless assets remain, but T025/T051/T057 and the composition test show the required terminal flow is not demonstrated.
inventory.md enumerates all ten baseline preset entries and records assets, runtime, installer/tests, shared dependencies and the PRESERVE/REMOVE decision.
Source assets are deleted, but install_support does not remove debt.py, full_cycle.py, their configs, policy or template from an existing installation.
Head preset registration is exactly one command, but normal update can retain removed runtime/configuration surfaces in an existing project.
install.sh and install.ps1 delegate to install.py; the shared clean-install path uses the one-entry preset and contains no removed-command copy wiring.
The clean package tree and copy allowlist exclude removed assets, but no test enumerates the actual post-Spec-Kit installed command registry as an exact set.
README and current-state documents present implement-review as the sole PowerPack command; removed pages are deleted and upstream commands are distinguished.
Remaining removed-command mentions are explicitly historical records, SPEC text or negative regression assertions.
Debt, full-cycle and probe-only tests are deleted while browserless, preflight, protocol and shared capability tests remain.
The offline collector does not exercise an installed registry exact-set, and T025/T051/T057 state that the minimum live operational flow remains unexecuted.
Registration equality exists, but test_baseline_contract.py never computes or asserts the required installed_powerpack_commands exact set.
Packaged defaults are clean, but default-preserving update leaves existing model-routing.json, prerequisites.json and removed dedicated configs untouched.
powerpack-tools doctor/update, shared runtimes, model routing, state/review paths and browserless provider modules remain composed.
The mandated clean-install behavioral invocation is absent; the new test only inspects argparse internals, while upgrades can retain runnable removed runtimes.
No removed preset entry or alias exists at HEAD, but unknown-command behavior is not invoked at the actual Spec Kit registration/dispatch layer.
reference-classification.md reports zero active source references, corroborated by the complete recursive GitHub tree for HEAD.
test_baseline_contract.py includes an explicit registration exact-set assertion tied to FR-017.
Dotted implement/converge templates are deleted; the preserved command names upstream commands and runtime prerequisite no longer reads an implement receipt.
All three entrypoints converge structurally on install.py, but their actual post-install inventories are not executed and compared.
Browserless runtime, smoke/preflight, deep-review protocol, default review configuration and supported documentation remain connected.
Probe script, probe documentation and probe-only test are deleted; supported smoke and preflight surfaces remain.
Full-cycle and technical-debt guides and their command-specific runtime, policy, template and configuration assets are deleted.
The expected alias ID maps to the FR-014 behavioral-removal contract; no actual removed-command dispatch invocation is tested.
Preset and package source are exact, but the generated integration command inventory is not enumerated after a real clean installation.
The recursive head tree and reference classification show no active current-tree removed-command asset or reference.
T025/T051/T057 explicitly state that terminal implement-review execution is outstanding; the composed test stops at mocked authentication.
Thin wrappers share install.py, but no evidence executes all three entrypoints and compares their resulting command inventories.
A registration regression guard exists, but tests were not executed in this review and the required installed-side guard is missing.
Clean source and copy allowlists exclude removed files, but a real installed state is not enumerated and upgrades retain legacy residue.
README, PROCESS_ARCHITECTURE and related current documents identify one current PowerPack command and label removed names as history or upstream.

verdict_challenge.strongest_counterexample: A user upgrades an existing supported PowerPack installation and assumes removed commands are gone, but overlay-only rematerialization leaves their runtimes and configuration on disk.
evidence: Base cli.py copied debt.py, full_cycle.py, debt/full-cycle configs, policy and template.

findings.title: Normal updates retain removed command runtimes and configuration
findings.evidence: The base install_support wrote debt.py, full_cycle.py, debt/full-cycle configs, policy/template and legacy routing/prerequisites. HEAD merely stops copying them. It never removes retired paths, while write_json at lines 54-58 preserves existing routing and prerequisites unless reset_config is explicitly true.
findings.failure_scenario: Upgrade a base-version project using normal or project-only update. Removed executables and files remain under .specify/powerpack, and old routing/prerequisite entries survive the overlay refresh.
findings.behavioral_impact: Removed capabilities remain on disk and stale configuration still describes them, violating FR-003, FR-012, FR-014 and the documented rematerialization contract.
findings.required_change: Add a versioned migration that removes known obsolete PowerPack-owned paths and prunes obsolete routing/prerequisite entries during normal refresh while preserving supported mutable settings and Project binding.
acceptance_criteria: Seed every artifact written by base install_support, refresh without --reset-config, and assert all retired managed paths are absent.
Assert routing has exactly implement-review and prerequisites use schema 2 implementation-evidence while supported mutable values remain.
Repeat refresh and prove migration idempotency.

findings.title: The immutable head cannot pass its own prerequisite or SC-003 gate
findings.evidence: T025, T051 and T057 remain unchecked and state that terminal live implement-review execution is outstanding. implement_evidence reads committed HEAD tasks and returns TASKS_INCOMPLETE for any open checkbox; the only composed test stops at mocked authentication.
findings.failure_scenario: Run prereq check for this exact PR head and active SPEC. It observes three unchecked tasks and exits 9 before convergence or review, preventing the required flow from reaching COMPLETE.
findings.behavioral_impact: User Story 2, FR-001, FR-010 and SC-003 remain incomplete, and the candidate is inadmissible under the predecessor contract it introduces.
findings.required_change: Execute and durably record the T025/T051/T057 flow, fix failures and commit truthful completion state; if those tasks are intentionally post-prerequisite, revise the durable lifecycle contract to remove the circular gate.
acceptance_criteria: Committed tasks.md contains zero unchecked task boxes without pre-marking unexecuted work complete.
Prerequisite check returns OK for the exact candidate head.
Durable evidence shows readiness, upstream convergence, quality gate, Sol review and browserless Project/GitHub review reach the terminal state.

findings.title: The installed exact-set contract is not tested
findings.evidence: test_installed_support_has_no_removed_command_assets calls install_support only, enumerates bin/*.py and checks selected support files. It never calls install_powerpack/install_components or enumerates installed PowerPack commands.
findings.failure_scenario: An installer or preset-materialization regression emits an extra command while source preset/support assertions remain satisfied, so the installed-side guard stays green.
findings.behavioral_impact: FR-010, FR-011, SC-001 and the install-side baseline contract lack mandatory composition-root proof.
findings.required_change: Exercise a clean canonical installation through the preset boundary and enumerate the resulting installed PowerPack command namespace.
acceptance_criteria: A test invokes the real installation composition or a faithful controlled Spec Kit fixture.
It asserts the installed command set equals exactly speckit.implement-review.
It fails when a second command is emitted or remains in the integration command directory.

findings.title: The behavioral removal check never invokes the real dispatcher
findings.evidence: test_removed_command_names_are_unknown_to_the_runtime_parser only inspects argparse choices and Python attributes. Removed preset commands such as full-cycle and debt-* were never powerpack.py top-level verbs.
findings.failure_scenario: A removed preset name survives as a generated command, alias or redirect while powerpack.py lacks an implement argparse verb; the test passes although direct invocation is not unknown.
findings.behavioral_impact: FR-014 and FR-015 are not validated at the command registration and dispatch layer where PowerPack commands are resolved.
findings.required_change: After a clean install, invoke representative removed command names through the actual Spec Kit resolver and assert unknown behavior with no implement-review side effect.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage invokes speckit.implement, speckit.full-cycle and at least one speckit.debt-* command.
Every invocation is rejected as unknown or nonexistent by the real resolver.
Rejected invocations create no review state, receipt or implement-review execution.
